engineeringScope: M2 sandbox authentication and account lifecycle

checks: Incorrect current password refused; provider password and audit unchanged
Password changed; old password refused, new password verified, one audit, current device preserved and other device denied
Wrong signed-in identity cannot accept invitation
New colleague creates provider identity and active administrator membership; used link refuses replay
Existing confirmed colleague joins correct workspace without creating a duplicate identity
Expired invitation renewed in UI; old token invalidated and new private link retained
Withdrawn link refused; reserved seat released; two accepted colleagues and owner reconcile to three seats
accounts.boundary: Actual browser journeys against disposable Auth with signup email confirmation required and captured locally. Application invitation email is deliberately unavailable and its private-link fallback is verified. External sending domains and configured OAuth remain separate.

hostedGoogle.baselinePreparation: A verified email-only identity was seeded on the retained owned sandbox fixture and password sign-in verified it before actual Google authentication. This is not a claim of a new email signup journey.
hostedGoogle.failureAttempt: One invitation sign-in submission stalled; reloading and retrying completed the journey. No root cause is attributed to that attempt.

providerFailureCoverage: Contract tests cover disabled/unavailable providers, foreign origins, unsafe return paths, missing/refused/unverified exchanges and explicit provider errors. Native hosted denial-callback replay refused protected entry; this does not simulate a Google outage or new consent denial.
launchReadiness: External sending-domain and delivery qualification, client-owned OAuth credentials and final handover remain separate gates. No production launch or final client acceptance is claimed.
privacy: No email addresses, invitation links, passwords, tokens, cookies or provider secrets are included. Temporary email/password fixture state was removed; the original Google owner workspace remains.
